origin: docs/CWE-352/javascript Common Pitfalls: Origin/Referer check that allows the request when the header is absent

finding.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
finding.summary: A cookie-authenticated state-changing transfer route relies on an Origin/Referer helper that allows requests with no header and has no CSRF token validation.

trap: Tightening the Origin/Referer helper while still allowing missing headers, or adding SameSite alone. The reported route remains a cookie-authenticated POST with no token that an attacker can submit cross-site when the browser sends cookies.
must_preserve: Authenticated successful transfers still call TransferLedger.scheduleTransfer() and respond with JSON containing status "scheduled" and transferId. Missing sessions still return 401 with the existing error shape, and cross-site failures still return 403 JSON rather than redirecting.
